Who a row belongs to, from the log

log_owner.Rd

The value of the newest write of owned_by signed by an account that holds the round's token, in the row's current life; the creator, as log_creators() names it, when none of them ever wrote one.

Usage

log_owner(events, record, creator, channel_account = NULL, before = NULL)

Arguments

events

The event log, as register_log() returns it.

record

The record id to look at.

creator

Who created the row, as log_creators() answers.

channel_account

The REDCap usernames that hold the round's token, one or more, or NULL when they are not configured.

before

A moment, "%Y-%m-%d %H:%M" in Rome and exactly that long, or NULL to read the whole log. A longer stamp, with seconds, would make a write of that same minute count as before it.

Value

One username; "" when no write of owned_by is believed and the creator is not known; NA_character_ when the log cannot say.

Details

The field itself is not believed. owned_by is @READONLY on the form, but an import draws no form: the import right is open to the referents, and an import writes the field as it writes any other. The log names who was authenticated for each write, so it says which value the round wrote, the same principle that names the creator from the log and not from requested_by.

The round's account is configured, decided on 2026-10-17, and without it, NULL, no write of owned_by is believed and the row belongs to its creator; a row whose log names two accounts writing the channel's fields is unknown then, log_channel_unknown(). Recognizing the round by what it writes would hand the row to a referent who imports owned_by alone on a colleague's new row before the round has written on it. With the account configured, a write of owned_by by any other account is ignored (decided on 2026-10-17): it names nobody, and the row stays with the owner the channel last wrote, or with its creator.

One write of another author is not ignored: a write of owned_by whose author is blank or missing, above the channel's write the owner is read from, or anywhere when there is none. It names nobody either, but it is not known to be somebody else's: it could be the channel's, so the answer is unknown, the direction that holds the row.

before asks who the row belonged to at a moment, and only what stands strictly before it counts. It is in the instance's civil time, which is Rome, the time the log's stamps are in, as for report_executions(): no conversion can move a write across it. A stamp of the row's log that does not read as one, log_stamp_reads(), makes the answer unknown, since the write it dates could stand on either side.

The newest write is read from the order of the answer, REDCap's own, newest first, as everywhere else in the log. A write by the channel that leaves the field blank names nobody, and the one below it is read.

The value is read whole, and not with log_value(), which stops at the first apostrophe: a UPN can hold one, so luca.d'amico would read luca.d, and the round would write that back as the owner and find it stable. The door writes owned_by alone, register_owner_import(), and REDCap logs only the fields an import changed, so the channel's event is owned_by = '<value>' and the value is everything between the first apostrophe and the last. The form is the one the rest of the log readers assume, field = 'value' with nothing escaped; how REDCap logs an apostrophe inside a value has not been measured. An event of the channel that wrote owned_by in any other form, beside other fields, makes the answer unknown: where one value ends and the next begins cannot be told from an apostrophe inside a name, and an unknown owner is the direction that holds the row.
